title: Which route to Iceberg fits you?

questions.q: Is Kafka already running in your company?
questions.hint: Think about whether other teams or tools read the same change feed.

options.label: Yes, and several systems read it
options.why: other systems already read your Kafka topics

options.label: Yes, but only for this job
options.why: Kafka would exist only for this one pipeline

options.label: No, and I would rather not add it
options.why: you want to avoid running Kafka

questions.hint: Free software still has a bill for servers and people.

options.label: A vendor hosts it for me
My team runs it on our servers

questions.q: Do you need to join or reshape data before it lands?

options.label: Yes, joins or filters in flight
options.why: you transform in flight, which Flink CDC and RisingWave are built for

options.label: No, copy it as it is

questions.q: Which source databases do you have?

options.label: Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB or SQL Server
options.why: your sources have CDC in most tools

options.label: Oracle, with change capture
options.why: you need Oracle CDC, which Debezium Server, Estuary and Flink CDC cover

options.label: A mix of databases and SaaS apps
options.why: you need SaaS sources, which Fivetran covers

questions.q: Who should handle Iceberg table upkeep?
questions.hint: Upkeep means compaction, which merges many small files into fewer big ones.

options.label: We will run it ourselves or with a separate product

kafka.name: Debezium on Kafka Connect with the Iceberg sink
kafka.summary: The classic route: Debezium puts changes in Kafka topics and the Apache Iceberg sink writes tables.
kafka.bestWhen: Kafka already runs and other systems read the same topics, or you want documented exactly-once delivery.
kafka.watchOut: you run Kafka, Kafka Connect and Debezium, and the sink page we read does not say how updates and deletes are applied.

dbzserver.name: Debezium Server with the community Iceberg sink
dbzserver.summary: Debezium's connectors with no Kafka, writing Iceberg through a community-maintained sink.
dbzserver.bestWhen: you want Debezium's connector list, including Oracle, without a broker.
dbzserver.watchOut: the sink is community maintained, upsert is off by default and each Server instance runs one connector.

flink.name: Flink CDC
flink.summary: Reads database changes inside Apache Flink and writes Iceberg, with room to reshape data in the same job.
flink.bestWhen: Flink already runs and you join or clean data before it lands.
flink.watchOut: you need a Flink cluster, source tables need primary keys and the Iceberg sink does not offer exactly-once.

risingwave.name: RisingWave
risingwave.summary: A streaming system with built-in database CDC and Iceberg sinks, driven by SQL.
risingwave.bestWhen: your team works in SQL and wants processing and Iceberg in one system.
risingwave.watchOut: it is a streaming system itself, and some features, such as direct SQL Server CDC, need a paid licence.

estuary.name: Estuary
estuary.summary: A hosted pipeline with log-based capture connectors and an Iceberg connector.
estuary.bestWhen: you want someone else to run the capture side and your lake is on Amazon S3.
estuary.watchOut: the REST connector needs a Spark job on Amazon EMR Serverless, and only S3-backed REST catalogs are supported.

fivetran.name: Fivetran Managed Data Lake Service
fivetran.summary: A hosted service that lands data as Iceberg tables, next to Fivetran's large connector list.
fivetran.bestWhen: Fivetran already moves your data, or you also need SaaS sources, and you want to run nothing.
fivetran.watchOut: it is hosted only, has no position deletes, and compaction is not listed.

dlt.name: dlt
dlt.summary: An open-source Python library that writes Iceberg through PyIceberg.
dlt.bestWhen: your team writes Python and the source is Postgres or a batch load.
dlt.watchOut: log-based CDC is Postgres only, Parquet only, and you write and watch the code yourself.

olake.name: OLake Go
olake.summary: Open-source software (Apache 2.0) that copies database changes into Apache Iceberg or Parquet with no Kafka or Debezium to run.
olake.bestWhen: your sources are Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB or SQL Server and you want a small setup.
olake.watchOut: jobs run on a schedule you set, and change capture covers PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, MongoDB and SQL Server (Oracle, Db2 and S3 load by full refresh or incremental).
